questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Limit of Sine or Cosine
questions.problem:
Consider the trigonometric function $f(x)=5sin⁡(2x).$

Current part:

Find ${lim}_{x\to \,\pi /4}f(x).$ If the limit does not exist, write "DNE" (without the quotation marks).

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        ${lim}_{x\to \,\pi /4}f(x)=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Substituting $x=\frac{\pi }{4}$ directly into the limit, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,\pi /4}f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \,\pi /4}5sin⁡(2x) \\  & =5sin⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{4}) \\  & =5\cdot sin⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =5\cdot 1 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Calculating the Average Rate of Change Over a Varying Interval where the Parameter Represents Distance
questions.problem:
Consider the trigonometric function $f(x)=5sin⁡(2x).$

Earlier part 1:

Find ${lim}_{x\to \,\pi /4}f(x).$ If the limit does not exist, write "DNE" (without the quotation marks).

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        ${lim}_{x\to \,\pi /4}f(x)=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        $5$

Earlier part 2:

Find ${lim}_{x\to \,\infty }f(x).$ If the limit does not exist, write "DNE" (without the quotation marks).

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        ${lim}_{x\to \,\infty }f(x)=$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        DNE

Current part:

What is the average rate of change of the function $f(x)$ over the interval $x\in [\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{\pi }{2}+h],$ where $h>0$ is a parameter? Express your answer in terms of $h.$

                            
                                    
                                        
                                            

                                                

                                        
                                        
                                        

                                    
                                
                                    
                                        
                                        $\frac{Δf}{Δx}\,=\,$

                                    
                                
                                    
                            
                                        {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
We have the function $f(x)=5sin⁡(2x).$ Notice that we are given the length $h$ of the interval. So, the average rate of change of $f$ over this interval is given by

$$
\frac{Δf}{Δx}=\frac{f(a+h)-f(a)}{h},
$$

with $a=\frac{\pi }{2}.$ Substituting into the formula and simplifying gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δf}{Δx} & =\frac{f(a+h)-f(a)}{h} \\  & =\frac{f(\frac{\pi }{2}+h)-f(\frac{\pi }{2})}{h} \\  & =\frac{5sin⁡(2(\frac{\pi }{2}+h))-5sin⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})}{h} \\  & =\frac{5sin⁡(\pi +2h)-5sin⁡(\pi )}{h} \\  & =\frac{5sin⁡(\pi +2h)-5(0)}{h} \\  & =\frac{5sin⁡(\pi +2h)}{h} \\  & =\frac{5}{h}sin⁡(\pi +2h).\end{aligned}
$$

g(h)=\frac{5}{h}sin⁡(\pi +2h).

questions.worked_solution:
The graph shows that as we approach $h=0$ from the left, the $y$ value approaches $-10.$ So, the left-hand limit is

$$
{lim}_{h\to \,{0}^{-}}g(h)=-10.
$$

Similarly, when we approach $h=0$ from the right, the $y$ value approaches $-10.$ So, the right-hand limit is

$$
{lim}_{h\to \,{0}^{+}}g(h)=-10.
$$

Since both the left and right-hand limits exist and are equal to $-10,$ we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{h\to \,0}g(h)=-10.
$$

$$

$$
{lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}\frac{1}{f(x)}={lim}_{x\to \,(\pi /2)^{-}}\frac{1}{5}csc⁡(2x)=\infty .

Find ${lim}_{x\to \,1}\frac{x-1}{{x}^{2}-3x+2}.$ If the limit does not exist, write "DNE" (without the quotation marks).

questions.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,1}\frac{x-1}{{x}^{2}-3x+2}=\frac{1-1}{(1)^{2}-3(1)+2}=\frac{0}{0}
$$

So, to find the limit, we have to factor the numerator and the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{x-1}{{x}^{2}-3x+2} & =\frac{x-1}{(x-1)(x-2)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{x-1}}{\cancel{(x-1)}(x-2)} \\  & =\frac{1}{x-2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,1}\frac{x-1}{{x}^{2}-3x+2} & ={lim}_{x\to \,1}\frac{1}{x-2} \\  & =\frac{1}{1-2} \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

questions.worked_solution:
In part 1, we found that 

$$
{lim}_{x\to \,\pi /4}f(x)=5.
$$

 

Applying the quotient rule, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,\pi /4}\frac{2f(x)}{(1+4x)^{3}} & =\frac{{lim}_{x\to \,\pi /4}(2f(x))}{{lim}_{x\to \,\pi /4}(1+4x)^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, 

* applying the constant multiple rule in the numerator, and 

* the root rule, followed by the sum rule in the denominator, 

we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{lim}_{x\to \,\pi /4}(2f(x))}{{lim}_{x\to \,\pi /4}(1+4x)^{3}} & =\frac{2\cdot {lim}_{x\to \,\pi /4}f(x)}{{({lim}_{x\to \,\pi /4}(1+4x))}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot {lim}_{x\to \,\pi /4}f(x)}{{(1+{lim}_{x\to \,\pi /4}(4x))}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 5}{{(1+4\cdot \frac{\pi }{4})}^{3}} \\  & =\frac{10}{(1+\pi )^{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$
